sources_read: psi-data/PSI-107/Presentations/PSI-107_Presentations_Laminar Smoke Points in Coflow Measured Aboard ISS.pdf

records.quote: SPICE is the first experiment that studies soot processes of laminar jet diffusion flame under long term microgravity condition with air coflow.
records.derivation: Section 'B. Air velocity distribution in the flow duct' (printed page 10). Not used as gravity evidence: the record-text objective/hypothesis sentences (objective statements only), the PSI label projectType 'Microgravity Investigation', and 'aboard the International Space Station' / 'in ISS MSG' (platform). The 'reduced gravity experiment in parabolic flight on board the KC-135 aircraft' (page 7) was a pre-flight camera-settings check, not SPICE science data, and is not proposed as a record.

records.quote: Smoke points of 55 microgravity gas-jet diffusion flames in coflowing air were measured in earth orbit.
records.derivation: Closing Remarks (printed page 18). The sentence names the smoke-point flames; all SPICE flames were flight tests ('The actual SPICE tests were conducted in SMG in twelve sessions from February 14, 2009 to June 23, 2009.', page 19). Side note, not a gravity issue: the smoke-point count differs across documents (55 here; 'Fifty-two' in the abstract, page 2; Table 1 on page 20 sums to 52).

records.test_id: ground tests in the same apparatus (Dotson 2009 thesis, ref. 7; no NASA test id; not in the PSI-107 table)
records.quote: The sooting propensity of the present fuels, identified from the smoke point lengths for fixed burner diameter and coflow velocity, generally increases from propane to ethylene, to 50% propylene, to 75% propylene, and to propylene. This is consistent with normal gravity results in the same apparatus.7
records.derivation: The trailing '7' is a superscript reference number: ref. 7 = Dotson, K.T., 'Smoke Points of Microgravity and Normal Gravity Coflow Diffusion Flames,' M.S. Thesis, Univ. of Maryland, 2009 (page 25). The Final Report only mentions these 1-g results; it gives no test ids or conditions for them. Ambiguous because the tests are reported second-hand and cannot be tied to any test id. The original (psi-data/PSI-107/Reports/PSI-107_Reports_SMOKE POINTS OF MICROGRAVITY AND  NORMAL GRAVITY COFLOW DIFFUSION  FLAMES_DotsonThesis.pdf) was outside this task's source list and was not read. Not used: 'However, testing in normal gravity8 has shown ...' (same page), because it cites ref. 8 (Kent and Wagner, 1984), an external work, not SPICE tests.

records.quote: The six bottles in one container are filled with six different fuel gases to the maximum safety pressure for that fuel: ethylene (210 psia), methane (210 psia), propane (110 psia), propylene (135 psia), 75% propylene (180 psia), 50% propylene (180 psia).
records.derivation: The psia values in this sentence are fuel-bottle fill pressures, NOT the test pressure; do not use them for 'pressure'. Corroborated by 'gas-jet diffusion flames' (R2, page 24).

Facility on the ISS. The SPICE apparatus installed in the MSG is a modified version of the apparatus built for Enclosed Laminar Flames (ELF) (Final Report page 9; see lineage). The sources read do NOT say that SPICE shares MSG flow-duct hardware with BASS, BASS-II or SLICE.

records.quote: Each flame was ignited in a controlled co-flow air environment, with burner diameters of 0.41 mm, 0.76 mm, and 1.6 mm and co-flow velocities ranging from 5.4 cm/s to 65 cm/s.
records.derivation: Burner diameters and co-flow velocities are already in the PSI table and are not extracted here.

records.quote: An important feature of SPICE is that it has air co-flow surrounding the flames.
records.derivation: Even at fan dial setting 0 a minimum air flow is kept in the duct (page 16), so no SPICE test is quiescent.

records.quote: Typical burn times were 60 s, and after each two such burns the MSG contents were flushed with ISS cabin air. The oxygen mole fraction of this cabin air is maintained within 19 – 24%.
records.derivation: Section 'SPICE FLIGHT TESTS' (printed page 13). This is the band within which ISS cabin air is kept, not a per-test O2 measurement. No O2 measurement inside the MSG is reported.

records.quote: Parameters ua [...] and Re assume conditions of 298 K, 101 kPa and 21±1% O2, and uniform velocity profiles.
records.derivation: Footnote a of Table 1. The words left out are ', uf,'. The PDF text layer splits the subscripted u_f across lines. This is the condition ASSUMED when computing air velocity, fuel velocity and Reynolds number, not a stated measurement of the test atmosphere. The source gives a tolerance of ±1, which is not written into 'numbers'. 21±1% falls inside the 19 – 24% cabin-air band of R9, so the two do not conflict and no DISCREPANCY is raised. The same footnote is repeated on presentation page 24.

records.quote: Parameters ua [...] and Re assume conditions of 298 K, 101 kPa and 21±1% O2, and uniform velocity profiles.
records.derivation: Same footnote as R10. 101 kPa is the pressure ASSUMED for the velocity and Reynolds-number calculations. No sentence in the sources read states the actual MSG or cabin pressure during the tests (see not_found).

records.quote: Typical burn times were 60 s, and after each two such burns the MSG contents were flushed with ISS cabin air. The oxygen mole fraction of this cabin air is maintained within 19 – 24%.
records.derivation: air: oxygen balanced mainly by nitrogen. Stream: AMBIENT (the co-flow air that fills the duct and the MSG). Not to be confused with the N2 in the 75% and 50% propylene fuel mixtures ('For mixtures the fuel mole fraction is shown and the inert is N2', page 20), which is in the FUEL stream.

not_found.looked_in: No source states the actual ambient (MSG or ISS cabin) pressure during the tests; R11 is only the 101 kPa calculation assumption. Searched: record text (all sections); Final Report PDF pages 1-28; presentation PDF pages 1-25. Pressures found but not applicable: fuel-bottle fill pressures (Final Report page 12, 110-210 psia; page 20, 'gage pressures of 760 – 1440 kPa'); mass-flow-controller standard conditions (page 12, 0 oC and 760 Torr); and earlier non-SPICE flames in the presentation (page 3 '1 Atm' 1-g background photo; pages 5-10 and 20, 30-130 kPa LSP/KC-135/STS data).

Test identifiers and conditions of the normal-gravity tests mentioned in R3: Final Report pages 1-28 (no ids or conditions given, only ref. 7); presentation pages 1-25 (the '1g TSI' values on page 22 are literature values, 'from Calcote and Manos', not SPICE tests). The Dotson thesis that should contain them was outside this task's source list.

lineage: SHARED_LINEAGE (stated): ELF. 'The SPICE project utilized and modified an apparatus constructed for a previous project, Enclosed Laminar Flames (ELF), which was conducted in the Middle Deck Glovebox of Space Shuttle Columbia during mission USMP-4/STS-87 in November, 1997.' (Final Report page 9). Program link with LSP: 'The original proposal of Professor Faeth was meant to be a supplement to the Laminar Soot Processes Experiment which was a combustion project under NASA Grant No. NAG3-1245, conducted onboard STS-73 and STS-94 in 1997.' (page 7). LSP still-air smoke points are plotted next to SPICE data (Final Report page 22, Fig. 18; presentation page 18). The sources read do NOT state that SPICE shares MSG flow-duct hardware with BASS, BASS-II or SLICE.
